answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, non-reusable deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A protocol slashes that deposit when a randomly audited job fails a verifiable check, while honest agents recover it after a challenge window. Creating a hundred identities then requires a hundred deposits, and spreading attacks across accounts does not dilute that cost. The oasis may host discovery, the pearl a valuable job, and the wharf the settlement point; none makes identities free.
